title: Ball Under a Parked Car
question: Your tee shot comes to rest underneath a parked car on the edge of the course. The car is preventing you from playing your ball. What is the correct ruling?

choices.text: You must play the ball as it lies.
You may move the car if it can be readily moved. If it cannot be readily moved, you are entitled to free relief.
You must take an unplayable ball with a one-stroke penalty.
You may always take free relief, whether the car can be moved or not.

explanation: A parked car is an obstruction. If the car can be readily moved, it is a movable obstruction: move the car and play the ball. If the car cannot readily be moved, it is treated as an immovable obstruction and you are entitled to free relief. This is covered by Rules 15.2a (Relief from Movable Obstructions) and 16.1 (Relief from Immovable Obstructions).
